## Owner-word issues carry the label `cockpit`

The label `owner-word` read as jargon to the people who open these issues. Owner-word issues now carry the label
**`cockpit`**; the older label **`owner-word`** still counts the same, so issues opened before the rename and apps
that still send it keep working.

- **Installer.** Creates the `cockpit` label on the forge when an authenticated `gh` can (outside CI); otherwise it
  prints the one command that creates it. An existing `owner-word` label is left as it is.
- **WORKFLOW §8.6, `rules/AGENTS.md`, `softure-worktree-manager`, `softure-doctor`.** Coordinators list open issues
  labelled `cockpit` or `owner-word`.
- **Routines.** The owner-word wake routine and the roadmap heartbeat read both labels; a wake routine prompt written
  before the rename names only `owner-word`, and `cockpit` counts the same. The package-update routine opens its
  owner-step issue with `cockpit`. The body marker `<!-- owner-word: {...} -->` is unchanged.

Adopting apps: re-run the installer (or create the label: `gh label create cockpit --color 5319e7 --description "An
owner decision the coordinator acts on (SOFTURE workflow)"`). A wake routine whose GitHub trigger filters by label
needs `cockpit` added to that filter in claude.ai/code/routines; a trigger without a label filter needs nothing.
